P.instruction: Using U, the clause decomposition, and the recursive modifier analysis, decide the complete plan of action.
P.value: 1. Identify the likely boundary: In a Google Apps Script doPost web app, returning HTML instead of JSON for a valid POST occurs at the outer Google Web App proxy / execution container boundary rather than inside ContentService. Specifically: (a) Uncaught fatal script error before or during compilation that bypasses ContentService and triggers Apps Script's default HTML error page; (b) Execution timeout (exceeding the maximum execution time limit), causing Apps Script infrastructure to terminate execution and return an HTML timeout error; (c) Authorization / login redirection (302 redirect to accounts.google.com when accessed without appropriate deployment permissions or cookie context); or (d) HTTP client failure to follow the 302 redirect from script.google.com to script.googleusercontent.com where ContentService serves the final payload. 2. Define the minimum diagnostic sequence: Step 1 (Client Inspection): Run curl with -i -L to capture HTTP status codes and headers, checking if a 302 occurs and whether the HTML body is an auth login page, Google infrastructure error, or Apps Script error page. Step 2 (Execution Log Check): Place console.log at the very first line of doPost(e); check Apps Script Executions log. If no entry exists, the boundary is pre-execution (Auth/URL). Step 3 (Top-level Catch): Wrap named-range read, new Function(), and invocation in a top-level try/catch that explicitly formats errors via ContentService.createTextOutput(JSON.stringify({error: err.toString(), stack: err.stack})).setMimeType(ContentService.MimeType.JSON). If HTML still returns despite the try/catch, the boundary is confirmed to be timeout or proxy/infrastructure. Step 4 (Duration Check): Log elapsed time to detect timeout truncation. 3. Preserve the architecture: Do not redesign or replace the named range, Function compiler, or doPost runtime.
